assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine, general reaction. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) enabled the scope. It is used daily in medicinal and process chemistry and appears in countless later syntheses, which is the kind of practical adoption I weigh most. It is a clear step beyond the earlier Pd cross-coupling prize (2010) in that it creates a different, pharmaceutically central bond.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic systems and the mechanistic understanding independently and in parallel in the mid-1990s onward. Kosugi (and Migita) reported earlier tin-amide aminations that were precursors but not general or catalytic in the later sense. I treat Kosugi as a precursor and propose the two main developers; the priority split relative to Kosugi, as I recall it, is a possible point of dispute.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of independent confirmation, extensive industrial scale use, and a stable mechanistic picture. Recognition is fully timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Exact credit for the earliest tin-amide work (Kosugi, Migita) versus the first truly catalytic amine coupling is from my memory and not verified here.
The 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members feel the area was already recognized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis gave synthetic chemists mild single-electron-transfer reactivity, enabling radical bond constructions that were difficult under thermal conditions, including dual catalysis with nickel and organocatalysts. The conceptual shift is clear and its adoption in late-stage functionalization and medicinal chemistry laboratories is very broad.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational 2008-2009 synthetic applications nearly simultaneously. Earlier photochemical antecedents (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, others) and later contributors (König, Nicewicz, Melchiorre) crowd the field, so a three-person limit makes the allocation contestable. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which may weigh against him.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years of widespread, independent replication; industrial uptake is real, though some applications are still maturing. Mostly timely, perhaps slightly early relative to the Pd amination.
uncertainties: MacMillan's prior Nobel may reduce the committee's appetite for recognizing him again.
Allocation among many strong contributors (Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz, König, Melchiorre) is unresolved.
Several of the photoredox reactions have limited process-scale use so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization lets chemists form C-C and C-heteroatom bonds directly from unactivated C-H bonds, shortening syntheses, which is exactly the efficiency theme I care about. Yu's ligand-enabled and template-directed selectivity solved the key problem of site control; Sanford and Hartwig added important Pd and Ir/B chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across a large field (Yu, Hartwig, Sanford, Smith, Daugulis, and others). I propose Yu for ligand and template control, Sanford for Pd(II/IV) and fluorination chemistry, and Hartwig for borylation (Smith and Hartwig jointly) but the best three is not obvious and some excluded contributors are strong.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted in academic synthesis and increasingly in industry, but many transformations still lack the generality and robustness of cross-coupling. Perhaps a few years from full maturity as a single clean story.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the prize story is C-H borylation, Pd-catalyzed directed C-H activation, or a combined concept.
Industrial process use remains narrower than for cross-coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered, non-quenched Lewis acid-base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without transition metals. This is a genuine conceptual novelty in main-group reactivity, with catalytic metal-free hydrogenation as the practical outcome.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free H2 activation (2006); Erker's group contributed key early follow-up and the intramolecular systems and broadened the concept. The two-person credit is clean and well documented, with Welch/Stephan as the initial report.
assessment.maturity: About 20 years of confirmation and a large literature, but synthetic impact on how chemists make molecules at scale is modest so far. Concept is mature; application is still limited.
uncertainties: Practical utility relative to conceptual novelty is a concern from a synthesis standpoint.
Whether others (for example Power, or earlier Wittig-Tochtermann and Brown observations) deserve mention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermolecular oxidative addition of alkane C-H bonds at an Ir(I) center (1982) showed that saturated C-H bonds can be cleaved by a homogeneous metal, a concept that underpins later catalytic C-H functionalization. It is conceptually crisp and historically important.
assessment.attribution: Bergman is the principal credited discoverer; Graham reported a closely related iridium result at nearly the same time, and others (Crabtree, Shilov earlier, Jones, Periana) contributed. A single-laureate proposal is simple but arguably incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Over 40 years of confirmation. Recognition would be late rather than premature, but the work did not directly yield a general synthetic method, which makes me rank it below catalytic C-H functionalization.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers rewarding the stoichiometric discovery or the later catalytic applications.
Credit relative to Graham, Shilov and Periana is not settled in my memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (Bertrand's phosphinocarbene 1988, Arduengo's imidazol-2-ylidene 1991) opened a new class of ligands and organocatalysts (NHCs). NHCs transformed Ru metathesis catalysts and Pd catalysis and are widely used in synthesis, so the effect on practical chemistry is concrete.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo and Bertrand are the clear discoverers. Subsequent NHC catalysis contributors (Nolan, Rovis, Bode) built on this, but the foundational isolation credit is two people, though Wanzlick's earlier conjectures are a historical wrinkle.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and broad adoption. Recognition is timely, with the risk that the importance is seen as spread over many downstream prizes (metathesis 2005).
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's carbene and Arduengo's NHC could be viewed as ambiguous.
Downstream impact is partly credited to others, such as the Grubbs catalysts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave living/controlled radical polymerization with predictable molecular weight and architecture using a simple Cu or Ru catalyst. It has had large impact on polymer synthesis and materials; for me the value is that it is a general, widely used method.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski (with Wang) and Sawamoto (with Kamigaito) reported the key discoveries independently in 1995. Wang is a co-author of the Matyjaszewski paper, and whether to include Wang or Sawamoto is a real allocation question. I propose Matyjaszewski, Sawamoto and Wang to honor the three-person cap but would prefer two.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, adopted globally. Competition from RAFT and nitroxide-mediated approaches complicates a single-method prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would reward ATRP alone or controlled radical polymerization more broadly with RAFT.
I am less able to judge polymer chemistry priority claims from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The phosphoramidite method made automated, reliable oligonucleotide synthesis possible, underlying PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a classic example of a synthetic chemistry method that quietly enabled other fields.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite chemistry on solid support in the early 1980s; Hood is credited for the automated instrument, which is more of an engineering contribution than the key chemical one. Earlier phosphotriester and phosphite-triester methods (Letsinger, Khorana) are part of the lineage. I propose Caruthers alone.
assessment.maturity: Over 40 years of use and confirmation; recognition would be late, which raises the possibility that other prizes (Khorana 1968, Sanger/Gilbert 1980, PCR) already covered the territory in the eyes of some members.
uncertainties: Whether the instrument versus chemistry contributions would be separated.
Overlap with earlier nucleic acid synthesis prizes and with the Letsinger and Khorana precursors.
